implementation_notes: Python has a single constructor signature and no overloads, so the creation owner is a classmethod alternative constructor - Order.from_cart(...), Order.reconstitute(row) - which the attrs documentation describes as a named constructor or factory method; a standalone factory class is then just a plain class used when creation needs repositories or external data translation. Invariants are enforced after field assignment by dataclasses __post_init__ (or attrs validators), and because nothing can stop a caller from invoking cls(...) directly, validation belongs in those hooks rather than in constructor privacy. Pydantic models take the same role declaratively: model_validate() is the factory that turns raw dictionaries into validated objects.
pitfalls: Nothing enforces the factory: Order(...) is always callable, so invariants must live in __post_init__/validators rather than in the factory by convention.
Mutable dataclass defaults shared between instances (use field(default_factory=...)) let constructed objects mutate each other's state.
frozen=True is shallow: a frozen dataclass can still hold a mutable list, so the collections an invariant depends on must be copied or frozen too.

variants.name: Declarative validated model (pydantic)
variants.implementation_notes: When raw data arrives as JSON or dicts, a declarative model can own the conversion end to end: define fields and validators once and make model_validate()/model_validate_json() the only path from raw data to a domain object, with failures returned as a structured ValidationError instead of scattered checks. It is a factory in the same sense - one owner enforcing invariants at birth - but declared rather than coded; keep behavior on the model's methods and reserve model_construct() for trusted reconstitution, because it deliberately skips validation.
pitfalls: model_construct() skips validation by design; it is a trusted reconstitution escape hatch, not a creation path.
Pydantic v1 and v2 APIs differ (parse_obj vs model_validate); a half-migrated codebase ends up with two creation owners.
A custom __init__ on a model silently disables validation parameters; use validators and model_post_init instead.
